name: Jon Ossoff
role: U.S. senator from Georgia (2021–present); documentary film executive; candidate for re-election in 2026
summary: Democratic senator who campaigns on health care affordability, Medicaid, labor rights, abortion and LGBTQ rights, voting rights and ending corporate money in politics. He supports the ACA with a public option over single payer, opposes Trump's tariffs and the 2025 budget law, and mixes strong border enforcement with support for legal status for long-resident immigrants. He backs the NATO alliance and has criticized Israel's conduct in Gaza and voted for some limits on arms sales while affirming Israel's security.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Supports the ACA with a strong public option and Medicaid expansion so every Georgian is insured, but has rejected Medicare for All; a public option is not a state guarantee for everyone.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Original cosponsor of the Raise the Wage Act ($15, indexed) and has said the minimum wage should be a living wage.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Mixed: backed 'lower taxes for all but the wealthiest' and opposed tax cuts for the wealthy, yet said in 2020 he did not support any increase in income tax rates.

unions-good.rationale: Cosponsored the PRO Act and said working people have faced a 'war on collective-bargaining rights'.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Pledged strong antitrust enforcement, reinstating Glass-Steagall and ending insurer and drug-company price gouging; introduced the Ban Corporate PACs Act.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

limit-guns.rationale: Supports universal background checks, red flag laws, closing the gun-show loophole and a ban on sales of semi-automatic rifles and high-capacity magazines, while saying he supports the Second Amendment; cosponsored the Background Check Expansion Act.

empower-police-military.rationale: Opposed defunding the police, but called for demilitarizing police and national use-of-force standards; as senator he secured funding for Georgia military installations.

rehabilitation.rationale: No stated position on the aim of prisons; reducing incarceration is something nearby.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Pledged to 'defend marriage equality' and said after Dobbs that the Court's reasoning threatens same-sex marriage; backs the Equality Act.

abortion-legal.rationale: Describes himself as pro-choice, pledged to confirm only judges who uphold Roe, and cosponsored measures to protect abortion and contraception access.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Called for a new Civil Rights Act to address systemic race and class bias in criminal justice and backs the John Lewis Voting Rights Act.

free-trade.rationale: Pledged to attack unfair overseas trade practices and reduce reliance on Chinese supply chains, but also wants businesses to compete globally and criticizes tariff chaos.

open-borders.rationale: Supports strengthening borders and enforcing immigration law alongside a path to legal status; open borders are not part of his platform.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Calls climate change a major threat and pledged massive federal investment in clean energy; voted for the Inflation Reduction Act; opposes the Green New Deal.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Says Trump's tariffs have been a disaster and pledged to repeal them.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Said he is strongly committed to Israel's security as a homeland for the Jewish people.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Backed deficit-financed COVID relief and $1,200 checks and said $600 was a joke; criticized tax cuts paid for by borrowing, but he has not stated a general view on deficits.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Campaigned on fighting corruption; said corporate money corrupts the legislative process and sponsored a congressional stock-trading ban.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Pledged equal rights and equal protection under law for all Americans regardless of gender or sexual orientation.

death-penalty.rationale: His 2020 campaign platform called for abolishing the death penalty.

collective-defense.rationale: Called NATO 'vital and inviolable' and reaffirmed the commitment to mutual defense of every member.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Defends NATO and multinational exercises and reaffirms mutual defense.

corporate-influence.rationale: Said corporate money corrupts the legislative process, refuses corporate PAC money, introduced the Ban Corporate PACs Act and backs ending Citizens United.

voter-id.rationale: Said in 2026 'Georgia has voter ID, and that's good'; no recorded position on a proof-of-citizenship requirement, and he opposed Georgia's 2021 election law.

free-public-college.rationale: Pledged to make public four-year degrees 'debt-free' and trade school free.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Supports a 'generous forgiveness program' for student loan debt, interest-rate caps and income-linked repayment.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Cosponsored the PRO Act, which lets contracts require all represented workers to pay representation fees and supersedes right-to-work laws.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Pledged to oppose efforts to re-impose a ban on openly gay service members.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Supports the Equality Act, which bars discrimination on gender identity; no detailed statement on legal recognition.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Opposed defunding the police ('the answer is to reform police') and abolishing ICE; backs prison oversight such as the Prison Camera Reform Act.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Pledged to attack anti-competitive special-interest subsidies secured by dominant firms with lobbying power.

ban-cartels.rationale: Pledged strong antitrust enforcement against dominant firms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Pledged to oppose legislation or executive action that undermines private communications and strong encryption.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Cosponsored the PRO Act, which expands protection for strikes and secondary actions and penalizes employers who retaliate.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: No stated position on individual pension accounts; protecting Social Security does not address privatisation.

flat-income-tax.rationale: No stated position on a flat tax; lower taxes for all but the wealthiest only implies one.

surveillance-ok.rationale: 2017 pledge to give agencies the resources to prevent terrorism 'without sacrificing privacy and human rights'; calls for a federal privacy law limiting surveillance.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: 2017 platform: oppose unnecessary military intervention and use force only where US national security is at stake.

strong-leader.rationale: He calls for restoring checks and balances against an unchecked president; campaign rhetoric about one president, not a stated view on strong leaders in general.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

state-directs-investment.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He explicitly defines Americans as a people united by convictions rather than ethnicity, ancestry or genes.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

separated-powers.rationale: He expressly endorses checks through three coequal branches and divided federal and state authority.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He opposes federal detention without cause and home raids without judicial warrants despite immigration-enforcement claims.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He condemns actors who ignore the rule of law or seize power through illegal means.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He treats an independent judiciary enforcing constitutional protections as essential even when political actors threaten those guarantees.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He praises constitutional guarantees of liberty and due process as binding protections enforced by independent courts.

elective-rulers.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

religious-nation.rationale: He defines shared American citizenship through civic values rather than one religious creed.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

property-franchise.rationale: He celebrates the extension of the franchise to Americans without land.

racial-franchise.rationale: He celebrates formerly enslaved people’s descendants gaining votes in a pluralist democracy.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He warns concentrated wealth purchases growing power over national affairs and defeats ordinary people’s interests.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: He criticizes Congress for ignoring nuclear annihilation and AI extinction risks while debating trivial priorities.

future-generations.rationale: He invokes responsibility to his daughters when opposing toxic contamination and ecological loss; rhetoric, not a direct statement of the principle.

collective-bargaining.rationale: He cosponsors the PRO Act and explicitly defends collective bargaining as necessary to give workers fair terms.

women-suffrage.rationale: He celebrates women gaining voting rights as an achievement of American democracy.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

notes:
Senate website pages cited were opened through Spanish-language mirror URLs; most ossoff.senate.gov URLs returned 403. Many quotes come via OnTheIssues compilations of his campaign sites and debates. Mixed on taxes: 2020 statements both favored lower taxes for all but the wealthiest and rejected income tax rate increases. Positions on the Laken Riley Act (voted yes January 2025, said it needed changes), Israel arms resolutions (voted for some, against others) and voting rights/filibuster were not matched to a statement or not clearly stated.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 23 answers taken from it, 21 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass; existing audit consulted only for notes and source list. Official hearing transcripts and legislation used instead of issue-score compilations. Whole career and all ten themes searched; priority Marxist statements are not answered from Democratic affiliation or criticism of corruption. None of the ten priority propositions has sufficiently specific evidence. Full 490 texts and remaining nulls reviewed. A nominee’s answers are not treated as Ossoff’s words. Opposition to particular AI health denials does not establish opposition to all algorithmic government. Nuclear expansion is a medium-confidence vote-based answer. His selective Israel arms votes are not converted into a general doctrine of nonintervention or international law. Criticism of warrantless raids does not imply unrestricted migration. No build or integration action undertaken. Specificity review left opposition to the January 6 attack insufficient for a categorical rule against all political violence, and public prison inspections insufficient for a general legal right to all government information. Further searches on monuments found only a request for careful consideration; searches on global economic redesign and Marxist propositions found no direct position.
